# Option reference

Every option dalforge reads, generated from the comments in its options
protos. [Writing the IDL](idl.md) explains how they fit together.

## `dal.v1`

`import "dal/v1/options.proto";`

| Option | On | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `(dal.v1.table)` | message | [Table](#dalv1table) |
| `(dal.v1.field)` | field | [Field](#dalv1field) |
| `(dal.v1.store)` | service | [Store](#dalv1store) |
| `(dal.v1.query)` | rpc | [Query](#dalv1query) |

### dal.v1.Table

Table configures the entity backing a message.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Table name. Defaults to the snake_case message name (HTTPRequestLog becomes http_request_log). It must be a valid unquoted identifier (DAL204); a default that's a reserved word, such as order or user, needs an explicit name. |
| `shard_key` | repeated `string` | Fields the data is sharded by. Recorded and validated (the fields must exist); dalforge doesn't route or enforce it. |

### dal.v1.Field

Field configures the column backing a field. Nullability comes from the proto field itself: proto3 `optional` fields are nullable, all others are required.

To remove a field, delete it and reserve its number and name. Its column is retired, not dropped: schema changes are always additive, so code from the previous release keeps working.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Column name. Defaults to the proto field name. |
| `format` | [Format](#dalv1format) | Refines a string field's type: it sets the Go type (e.g. uuid.UUID for FORMAT_UUID) and the column type. |
| `primary_key` | `bool` | Marks the field as part of the primary key. Multiple fields form a composite key, ordered by their declaration order in the message. A FORMAT_UUID key left nil in a create is assigned a UUIDv7. |
| `unique` | `bool` | Makes the column unique. On an entity with ROLE_DELETE_TIME it's unique among live rows only, so a soft-deleted row doesn't block its value. |
| `role` | [Role](#dalv1role) | Behaviour the generated code manages for this column. |

### dal.v1.Store

Store binds a service to the entity whose access patterns it declares.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `entity` | `string` | Fully qualified or file-local name of the entity message, e.g. "Order". |

### dal.v1.Query

Query declares the access pattern implemented by one rpc.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get` | [Get](#dalv1get) | One of `kind`. |
| `list` | [List](#dalv1list) | One of `kind`. |
| `create` | [Create](#dalv1create) | One of `kind`. |
| `update` | [Update](#dalv1update) | One of `kind`. |
| `delete` | [Delete](#dalv1delete) | One of `kind`. |
| `upsert` | [Upsert](#dalv1upsert) | One of `kind`. |

### dal.v1.Get

Get fetches at most one row by a unique key.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `by` | repeated `string` | Lookup fields. Defaults to the primary key. Any other set must be covered by a unique field or unique index. |
| `consistency` | [Consistency](#dalv1consistency) | Which copy of the data the read may use. Defaults to eventual. |

### dal.v1.List

List pages through rows matching equality filters, using keyset pagination: the access path is (eq..., order_by..., primary key).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `eq` | repeated `string` | Equality filter fields. |
| `range` | `string` | Optional range filter field. It must be the leading order_by field. The filter is half-open: the request carries &lt;range>_from (inclusive) and &lt;range>_to (exclusive), both required. |
| `order_by` | repeated `string` | Sort fields, each optionally suffixed with ASC or DESC. When empty, the sort is inherited from a backend-declared index whose leading fields are exactly eq; failing that, it is the primary key. The primary key is always appended as the keyset tie-breaker. |
| `default_page_size` | `uint32` | Page size used when the caller passes 0. Zero here means 50. |
| `max_page_size` | `uint32` | Largest page size; bigger requests are clamped. Zero here means 500. |
| `consistency` | [Consistency](#dalv1consistency) | Which copy of the data the read may use. Defaults to eventual. |

### dal.v1.Create

Create inserts one row and returns it. Every field of its parameters is a pointer, and nil means the column default, NULL, a new UUIDv7 key, or a missing-field error, depending on the field.

No fields.

### dal.v1.Update

Update modifies one row by primary key. When the entity has a ROLE_VERSION column the update is a compare-and-swap on it.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `columns` | repeated `string` | Fields the update may set. Defaults to every non-key field that is not managed by a Role. |

### dal.v1.Delete

Delete removes one row by primary key. When the entity has a ROLE_DELETE_TIME column the delete is soft.

No fields.

### dal.v1.Upsert

Upsert inserts one row, or updates it on conflict. The last writer wins (the version is bumped without a compare-and-swap), and a soft-deleted row is never revived.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `conflict_on` | repeated `string` | Conflict target fields. Defaults to the primary key; any other set must be covered by a unique field or unique index. |
| `columns` | repeated `string` | Fields updated on conflict. Defaults to the same set as Update.columns. |

### dal.v1.Format

Format is a logical type layered on a proto scalar.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `FORMAT_UNSPECIFIED` | Unset. |
| `FORMAT_UUID` | On string: a UUID. Prefer UUIDv7 for primary keys. |
| `FORMAT_DECIMAL` | On string: an arbitrary-precision decimal. |
| `FORMAT_JSON` | On string: a JSON document. |

### dal.v1.Role

Role marks columns whose values the generated code manages.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `ROLE_UNSPECIFIED` | Unset. |
| `ROLE_CREATE_TIME` | On a google.protobuf.Timestamp: set to now() on insert, never updated. |
| `ROLE_UPDATE_TIME` | On a google.protobuf.Timestamp: set to now() on insert and on every update. |
| `ROLE_DELETE_TIME` | On an optional google.protobuf.Timestamp: soft delete. Delete sets it, and every generated statement ignores rows where it is set. |
| `ROLE_VERSION` | On a required int64 (or int32): optimistic locking. It starts at 1, and every update is a compare-and-swap on it that increments it. |

### dal.v1.Consistency

Consistency is the read consistency an rpc needs.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `CONSISTENCY_UNSPECIFIED` | Unset: eventual. |
| `CONSISTENCY_EVENTUAL` | Eventual: Postgres reads from the reader pool, which may lag the writer slightly; DynamoDB does an eventually consistent read. |
| `CONSISTENCY_STRONG` | Strong, for read-after-write: Postgres reads from the writer pool; DynamoDB sets ConsistentRead (not available on secondary indexes). |

## `dal.pg.v1`

`import "dal/pg/v1/options.proto";`

| Option | On | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `(dal.pg.v1.file)` | file | [File](#dalpgv1file) |
| `(dal.pg.v1.table)` | message | [Table](#dalpgv1table) |
| `(dal.pg.v1.column)` | field | [Column](#dalpgv1column) |

### dal.pg.v1.File

File states what the schema in a file needs from Postgres. The deploy target itself (e.g. 16.9) lives in dalforge.yaml; lint fails when the target is older than min_version or lacks a declared extension.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `min_version` | `uint32` | Minimum Postgres major version, e.g. 16. Zero means dalforge's floor. |
| `extensions` | repeated `string` | Extensions the schema needs, e.g. ["vector"]. Each one is emitted as CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS, and every custom_type it provides must be covered by one of them. |

### dal.pg.v1.Table

Table refines the Postgres table.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `indexes` | repeated [Index](#dalpgv1index) | Explicit indexes. Most indexes are derived from access patterns; declare one here only for partial or covering indexes, or to pin the sort order that List queries without order_by inherit. |
| `index_budget` | `uint32` | How many indexes (the primary key, unique columns and list indexes) the table may have before DAL201 warns: each one adds write cost. Zero means the default, 5. |

### dal.pg.v1.Index

Index is an explicitly declared index.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Index name. Defaults to &lt;table>_&lt;col>_&lt;col>_idx. |
| `columns` | repeated `string` | Key fields (proto field names) in order, each optionally suffixed with ASC or DESC, e.g. ["account_id", "created_at DESC"]. |
| `include` | repeated `string` | Non-key fields stored in the index (INCLUDE) for index-only scans. |
| `where` | `string` | Predicate for a partial index, as a SQL boolean expression. A list uses a partial index only if this is exactly its own filter (deleted_at IS NULL); otherwise it's for custom queries. |
| `unique` | `bool` | Makes the index unique. A unique index can back a get.by or an upsert.conflict_on on its columns (DAL104). |

### dal.pg.v1.Column

Column refines the Postgres column.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | [Type](#dalpgv1type) | One of `pg_type`. A first-class Postgres type. Only types that fit the field's proto type are allowed (DAL209), since the Go type follows the proto type. |
| `custom_type` | `string` | One of `pg_type`. Raw type for anything Type doesn't cover (extension types such as vector(1536), or parameterised types such as numeric(12,2)). |
| `default` | `string` | Column default as a SQL expression, e.g. "now()" or "'pending'". |
| `go_type` | `string` | Go type for a custom_type column, as "import/path.Type", e.g. "github.com/pgvector/pgvector-go.Vector". It's passed to sqlc as a type override and becomes the model field's type. Required with custom_type. |

### dal.pg.v1.Type

Type lists Postgres types with first-class support: the generator knows their Go type, pgx codec, sqlc override and keyset encoding. Values are only ever added. A value whose type needs a newer Postgres than the floor notes it, e.g. "// PG 17+". All values below exist in every supported version.

Values: `TYPE_TEXT`, `TYPE_UUID`, `TYPE_BOOLEAN`, `TYPE_SMALLINT`, `TYPE_INTEGER`, `TYPE_BIGINT`, `TYPE_REAL`, `TYPE_DOUBLE_PRECISION`, `TYPE_NUMERIC`, `TYPE_TIMESTAMPTZ`, `TYPE_DATE`, `TYPE_JSONB`, `TYPE_BYTEA`, `TYPE_INET`. Zero (`TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`) means unset.
